sentences.text: 1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 15.05.2023.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 15.05.2023 at about 5-30 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Kengeri Traffic Police Station, in the traffic signal of Jnanabharathi circle, when the Petitioner stopped the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EQ- 5959 at the traffic signal in order to proceed towards Bangalore University, at that time the driver/accused M.V.C.No.3388/2023 3 SCCH - 7 drove the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-6019 from Mysore main road,
Rajarajeshwari Gate towards Kengeri in a rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and at Jnanabharathi circle dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result the Petitioner fall on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his left hand.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Sparsh Hospital wherein he was treated as inpatient and undergone surgery therein and he has spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenditure and other incidental charges.
In this regard the informant/Pavan C. Raj has lodged complaint before the Kengeri Traffic police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.162/2023 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279, 337 & 338 of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

3. Further it is contended that, prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was aged about 32 years and he was working Software Engineer at Private company and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m. Due to the injuries sustained in the M.V.C.No.3388/2023 4 SCCH - 7 alleged accident he lost his income and future prospective life, happiness, and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-6019.
Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.
4. In response to the notice, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.

5. In the written statement of respondent No.2, Respondent No.2 the Insurance Company has admitting that, the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-6019 was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part.

Further it is Madhusudhan.M vs Ravi Kiran on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101421773/
2 contended that the insured vehicle is not involved in the accident.

Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section M.V.C.No.3388/2023 5 SCCH - 7 134(C), 158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further it is contended that the alleged accident is occurred due to sole negligence and fault of the petitioner and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to get compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. Act., and violated terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.
:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-6019 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
M.V.C.No.3388/2023 6 SCCH - 7 (3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
(4) What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case of petitioner, petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex.P-1 to P.16 and Ex.P-24, Medical Record Office of Sparsh Hospital examined as PW-2 and got marked Ex.P.17 to Ex.P-21, Dr. Nagaraj B.N., got examined as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.22 and Ex.P.23 and closed their side.

The petitioner in the petition has contended that, on 15.05.2023 at about 5-30 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Kengeri Traffic Police Station, in the traffic signal of Jnanabharathi circle, when the Petitioner stopped the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EQ- 5959 at the traffic signal in order to proceed towards Bangalore University, at that time the driver/accused drove the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-6019 from Mysore main road, Rajarajeshwari Gate towards Kengeri in a rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and at Jnanabharathi circle dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result the Petitioner fall on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his left hand.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Sparsh Hospital wherein he was treated as inpatient and undergone surgery therein.
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The Respondent No.2/Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle and therefore he cannot M.V.C.No.3388/2023 8 SCCH - 7 be held to be negligent.
Further it is alleged that the driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
12.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.

Hence, in order to prove his case,
the Petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.16 and Ex.P-24 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.

In support of the Petitioner's case and in order to substantiate the oral evidence of P.W.1, the Petitioner has examined another two witnesses by name Sateesh Kumar.B.R., as Pw.2, by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N., as PW.3.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.
Ex.P-1 is the M.V.C.No.3388/2023 9 SCCH - 7 True copy of FIR, Ex.P-2 is the True copy of complaint,

Ex.P-3 is the true copy of the spot Panchanama and spot sketch, Ex.P.4 is the Statement of Victim,
Ex.P-5 and 6 are the Statements of eye witnesses, Ex.P-7 and Ex.P-8 are the IMV reports, Ex.P-9 is the Notice issued under Section 133 of MV Act, Ex.P-10 is the Reply to Notice, Ex.P-11 is the Charge Sheet, Ex.P-12 is the Order sheet in CC No.5860/2023, Ex.P-13 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P-14 is the Discharge Summary, Ex.P-15 is the Adhar Card, Ex.P-16 is the driving licence and Ex.P-24 is the medical bills.
13.

In the cross-examination of PW-1 by the counsel for Respondent No.2, he has deposed that he is possessing valid and effective driving licence to ride the unoffending vehicle and the said vehicle is duly insured.

At the time of accident he was proceeding towards Bengaluru University and at University traffic signal he has stopped the unoffending vehicle and when there was red signal the Madhusudhan.M vs Ravi Kiran on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101421773/

4 driver of the offending car vehicle drove the same in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and without cautious of the traffic signal dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result he has sustained grievous injuries and thereafter he was shifted to Sparsh M.V.C.No.3388/2023 10 SCCH - 7 Hospital.

Further he has denied that at the spot he drove the unoffending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and at the traffic signal he has suddenly applied the break and stopped the vehicle, as a result the following unoffending vehicle dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle.
Further he has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to high speed negligence and fault and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further he has deposed that he has narrated the alleged incident to the hospital and he has undergone surgery therein.

Further he has denied that due to alleged accident he has sustained simple injuries and now he is hale and healthy and he has not suffering any pain or difficulties to do his regular work and activities as past.
Further he has deposed that he has undergone.
Further he has denied that he has not incurred Rs.1,82,000/- towards his medical expenditure and the said amount is incurred by the insurance company.
Further he has denied that further he has not taking follow-up treatment.
Further he has deposed that he is working as Software Engineer and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m., and he has not produced any documents in that regard.
Further he has denied that he is able to do work as past.

Further he has denied M.V.C.No.3388/2023 11 SCCH - 7 that in order to get more compensation in collusion with the police he has falsely implicated the driver of the offending vehicle and registered false case against him and he has produced concocted created documents and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.
During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case and he has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

14. In the examination in chief of PW.2 he has deposed that he is working as Medical Record Officer of Sparsh Hospital and he has produced Ex.P-17/Authorization letter, Ex.P-18/MLC Extract,
Ex.P-19/Police Intimation, Ex.P-20/ Charge Sheet and Ex.P-21/X-ray Films.
In the cross-examination of PW-2 he denied that in order to help the Petitioner and in collusion with him he has produced concocted documents and deposing false.

15. The Respondent No.2 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police and in order to prove its version the Respondent No.2 has neither stepped into the witness box nor produced documents and any how the Respondent No.2 cross- examined the PW-1 to PW-3.

On careful reading of Ex.P7 and Ex.P-8/Motor Vehicle Accident Inspection Reports it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident did not occur because of the mechanical defects in respect of the said offending vehicle.
Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle and opined that, left side portion of the front bumper damaged.
Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the unoffending vehicle and opined that, rear registration number plate damaged and left side crash guard scratched.

17. On going through the Ex.P-13/Wound Certificate it is seen that the Doctor opined that the Petitioner was treated at Sparsh Hospital and in the said alleged accident the Petitioner has Madhusudhan.M vs Ravi Kiran on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101421773/
5 sustained 1) Abrasion of left knee and 2) fracture of left radius.
Further the doctor opined that the injury No.1 is simple in nature and injury No.2 is grievous in nature.

18. On going through the Ex.P-2/Complaint it is seen that on 15.05.2023 at about 5-30 p.m., in the traffic signal of Jnanabharathi circle, when the Petitioner stopped the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EQ- 5959 at the traffic signal in order to proceed towards Bangalore University, at that time the driver/accused M.V.C.No.3388/2023 13 SCCH - 7 drove the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-6019 from Mysore main road, Rajarajeshwari Gate towards Kengeri in a rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and at Jnanabharathi circle dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle, as a result the Petitioner fall on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his left hand.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Sparsh Hospital wherein he was treated as inpatient and undergone surgery therein.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

19. On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar along with spot sketch it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/complaint, on 17.05.2023, informant/Pavan C. Raj showed the place of incident to the police.

The police have conducted the detailed spot mahazar in the presence of panch witnesses and prepared spot Sketch.
20.

Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that,
Petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed the said Accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to M.V.C.No.3388/2023 14 SCCH - 7 fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent and the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, mahazar, Spot Sketch, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, M.V.C.No.3388/2023 15 SCCH - 7 the accused drew the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle in which the petitioner was stopped the unoffending vehicle due to traffic signal, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P3/spot Mahazar, Ex.P-7 and Ex.P-8/MVA reports, Ex.P-9 and Ex.P-10/ Notice issued under Section 133 of MV Act and Reply to Notice, Ex.P-11/Charge Sheet and Ex.P- 13/Wound Certificate clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.

It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained Madhusudhan.M vs Ravi Kiran on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101421773/
6 grievous injuries in the alleged incident.

Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that,
the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P13/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

Thus because of such negligent act M.V.C.No.3388/2023 16 SCCH - 7 of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2 and 3:-

The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that the injured Petitioner was aged about 32 years and he was working as Software Engineer and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m., and the Petitioner has incurred heavy expenses towards medical expenditure.

As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony,
medical expenses, special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

22. On the other hand the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.25,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the M.V.C.No.3388/2023 17 SCCH - 7 Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

23. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 32 years and he relied on the Ex.P.16/ driving licence of the Petitioner, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 18.05.1991 and this accident was took place on 15.05.2023.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 31 years 11 months.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 31 years.
24. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was working as Software Engineer and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
But he has not produced single piece of documents to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the Petitioner taken at Rs.15,250/-.

In the chief examination of PW-3/Dr.Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has sustained left radius mid shaft fracture and the Madhusudhan.M vs Ravi Kiran on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101421773/
7

Petitioner undergone ORIF with plate and screws on 16.05.2023 and the Petitioner now complains of pain in the left forearm, unable to rotate the forearm, unable to lift weight and carry his work as software engineer and on examination the Petitioner has healed scar over the left forearm, wasting of the left forearm muscles, restricted forearm muscles and recent X-ray of the left forearm shows united fracture with implant in situ and the Petitioner has sustained total disability of the left arm at 39% and whole body disability at 13%.
In support of his oral evidence, the doctor/PW-3 has produced Ex.P-22/Clinical notes and Ex.P-23/X-rays.
In the cross-examination of PW-3 by the counsel for Respondent No.2 he has deposed he has not treated doctor of the Petitioner.
Before assessing the disability he has not gone through the case sheet of the Petitioner and he has not taken advice of the treated doctor.
He has perused Discharge Summary.
The Petitioner has sustained fracture and same is simple fracture (closed).
Now the fracture is united.
Further he has denied that M.V.C.No.3388/2023 19 SCCH - 7 as fracture is united the disability will not arise.
Further he has deposed that Petitioner can do his normal activities.
Further he has denied that the disability and mobility components of the Petitioner is in normal.
Further he has denied that though the range of movements of the Petitioner is normal.
He has falsely assessed the disability.
Further he has denied that he has falsely assessed the disability at 13% to the whole body.
Further he denied that in order to help the petitioner he has assessed disability on the higher side and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

26. As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as working as Software Engineer while doing his work the petitioner has to stand and sit for long time, he has to bend, put weight on both legs, he has to sit down while doing the work.
But due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident the petitioner has not in position to do work as past.
The doctor has assessed the total disability of the left arm at 39% and whole body disability at 13%.
Hence by considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 13% to the whole body.
. With regard to the quantum, the age of the petitioner is considered as 31 years and the income is considered at Rs.15,250/- p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 16 is applicable and functional disability is considered at 13%.

On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner,
the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs.15,250/- X 12 X 16 X 13/100) = Rs.3,80,640/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.3,80,640/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.

28. In the alleged accident the petitioner has sustained left radius mid shaft fracture and the Petitioner undergone ORIF with plate and screws on 16.05.2023, which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering, mental agony.

29. Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Sparsh Hospital for a period from 15.05.2023 to 17.05.2023, i.e., for a period of 3 days.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.9,000/- (Rs.3,000/- per day X 3 days) under head of special diet and conveyance.

Madhusudhan.M vs Ravi Kiran on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101421773/
8 M.V.C.No.3388/2023 21 SCCH - 7 30.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
31. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast three months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.45,750/- (Rs.15,250/- x 3 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
32. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical expenses as per Ex.P.24 for an amount of Rs.1,82,886/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,82,886/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.

33. The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:

9,000-00 4 Loss of amenities 50,000-00 5 Loss of income during laid up period 45,750-00 M.V.C.No.3388/2023 22 SCCH - 7 6
Actual medical expenses 1,82,886-00 Total 7,18,276-00 34.

The Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,18,276/-.
35.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 and 3 are partly in the affirmative.
36. Issue No.4:

In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.7,18,276/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Eighteen Thousand M.V.C.No.3388/2023 23 SCCH - 7 Two Hundred and Seventy Six only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

opennyai_summary.facts:
1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 15.05.2023.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-6019.
Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL, permit and other documents as per the law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section M.V.C.No.3388/2023 5 SCCH - 7 134(C), 158(6) of M.V. Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-6019 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the claim petition?
M.V.C.No.3388/2023 6 SCCH - 7 (3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
(4) What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Respondent No.2/Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle and therefore he cannot M.V.C.No.3388/2023 8 SCCH - 7 be held to be negligent.
The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed the said Accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to M.V.C.No.3388/2023 14 SCCH - 7 fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent and the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony,
medical expenses, special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.
Since the M.V.C.No.3388/2023 17 SCCH - 7 Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
23. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 32 years and he relied on the Ex.P.16/ driving licence of the Petitioner, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 18.05.1991 and this accident was took place on 15.05.2023.
24. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was working as Software Engineer and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, M.V.C.No.3388/2023 15 SCCH - 7 the accused drew the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle in which the petitioner was stopped the unoffending vehicle due to traffic signal, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P13/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Thus because of such negligent act M.V.C.No.3388/2023 16 SCCH - 7 of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
But he has not produced single piece of documents to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income as to be assessed.
opennyai_summary.decision:
On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner,
the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs.15,250/- X 12 X 16 X 13/100) = Rs.3,80,640/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.3,80,640/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.
29. Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Sparsh Hospital for a period from 15.05.2023 to 17.05.2023, i.e., for a period of 3 days.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.9,000/- (Rs.3,000/- per day X 3 days) under head of special diet and conveyance.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
31. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast three months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.45,750/- (Rs.15,250/- x 3 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
32. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical expenses as per Ex.P.24 for an amount of Rs.1,82,886/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,82,886/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.
33. The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
Sl. Compensation under different heads Amount in No. (Rs) 1 Loss of future income due to disability 3,80,640-00 2 Pain and suffering, mental agony 50,000-00 3
Special
conveyance
9,000-00 4 Loss of amenities 50,000-00 5 Loss of income during laid up period 45,750-00 M.V.C.No.3388/2023 22 SCCH - 7 6
Actual medical expenses 1,82,886-00 Total 7,18,276-00 34.
The Petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,18,276/-.
35.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 and 3 are partly in the affirmative.
36. Issue No.4:
In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.7,18,276/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Eighteen Thousand M.V.C.No.3388/2023 23 SCCH - 7 Two Hundred and Seventy Six only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
